subject: Biotechnology
title: What Is Synthetic Biology
description: Learn What Is Synthetic Biology in one minute.

hook.text: If biology is hardware, DNA is the code — synthetic biology writes new programs for living cells from scratch.

buildup.text: Engineers design biological parts with standardized functions — promoters, ribosome binding sites, terminators.

discovery.text: These parts snap together like Lego bricks — composable genetic programs that cells execute faithfully.

twist.text: Biology is messy — cells mutate, evolve, and break engineered circuits. Reliability is the biggest challenge.

climax.text: The global synthetic biology market exceeded $15 billion in 2023 — from lab curiosity to industrial reality.

punchline.text: Design life like software — synthetic biology programs cells.

quiz.question: What is the biggest challenge in synthetic biology?
options: DNA synthesis is too expensive for commercial use
Living cells mutate and evolve, breaking engineered circuits over time
No standardized biological parts exist yet

takeaways: Synthetic biology applies engineering design principles to living systems
Standardized genetic parts enable modular construction of biological systems
The goal is making biology as predictable and programmable as electronics

faq.question: How is synthetic biology different from genetic engineering?
faq.answer: Genetic engineering typically modifies existing organisms by adding or changing individual genes. Synthetic biology takes an engineering approach, designing entire systems from standardized parts with predictable behavior. It emphasizes modularity, abstraction, and rational design principles.

faq.question: What are the core principles borrowed from engineering?
faq.answer: Standardization creates interchangeable parts with defined interfaces. Abstraction separates system levels so designers work at the appropriate complexity. Modularity ensures parts function independently and combine predictably. These principles aim to make biology designable.
